editorial.titleTr: Criminal justice overhaul shifts into high gear without a driver
summaryTr: The abolition of the Prosecutor's Office will disperse investigative authority among the police, the public prosecution office, and the serious crimes unit.
Concerns about chaos are growing due to leadership vacancies and institutional instability.
Investigative delays are anticipated due to shortages in personnel, legal frameworks, and computer systems.
editorial.bodyTr: Starting October 2nd, the prosecution office has been abolished, with the police, public prosecution office, and serious crimes investigation unit dividing responsibilities among themselves. Worries have emerged that inadequate preparation in personnel, legal frameworks, and computer systems could lead to investigative delays and conflicts between agencies.

editorials.body: ① 트럼프 대통령은 알래스카 LNG 참여가 결정됐다고 발표했으나 한국 정부는 투자 동의가 없었다고 했습니다. ② 알래스카 LNG 사업은 공사 난도가 높고 초기 비용이 크며 수익성도 불확실해 미국 기업도 철수한 적이 있습니다. ③ 합의문은 조건을 전제로 검토만 하기로 했으니 정부는 투자 조건과 손실 위험을 따져 국익을 지켜야 합니다.

editorials.titleTr: Alaska LNG Investment: U.S. Unilateral Move, Korea Must Protect National Interests
summaryTr: President Trump unilaterally announced a decision to participate in Alaska LNG, but South Korea has not agreed to invest.
It is a project from which American companies have withdrawn due to high construction difficulty, massive initial costs, and uncertain profitability.
The government must carefully review investment conditions and loss risks to protect national interests.
editorials.bodyTr: President Trump announced that South Korea's participation in the Alaska LNG project had been decided, but the Korean government said there was no investment agreement. The Alaska LNG project has high construction difficulty, substantial upfront costs, and uncertain profitability, which has led even American companies to withdraw from it in the past. The agreement stipulates only conditional review, so the government must protect national interests by carefully examining investment conditions and loss risks.

summaryTr: Implementation of judicial reform transferring prosecutorial investigative authority to the Major Crimes Investigation Agency.
Investigation gaps become inevitable due to vacant leadership positions and insufficient personnel.
Concerns that administrative shortcomings could lead to public harm through resulting confusion.
editorials.bodyTr: The judicial restructuring that transferred the nation's core investigative functions from the prosecution to the Major Crimes Investigation Agency has been implemented. However, due to vacant leadership positions at major institutions, insufficient personnel, and delays in system construction, investigative gaps are inevitable. Concerns have been raised that confusion resulting from administrative shortcomings and delayed jurisdiction adjustments could directly harm the public.

editorial.title: [사설] DMZ 지뢰 폭발, ‘불의의 사고’ 아닌 ‘북한의 도발’이다
editorial.body: 입력 종합 26면 이재명 대통령은 어제(1일) 국군의날 기념식에서 열흘 전 우리 장병 3명이 북한이 비무장지대(DMZ)에 매설한 지뢰 폭발로 중경상을 입은 사건을 언급하며 “불의의 사고”라고 표현했다. 북한의 정전협정 위반에 대한 규탄도 없었고, 김여정 노동당 부장의 ‘자작극’ 주장에 대한 반박도 없었다. 대신 이 대통령은 “정부는 남북 간 군사적 긴장을 낮추기 위한 실질적인 조치를 일관되게 이어 나가겠다”고 밝혔다. 우선 이 대통령의 발언은 그제 북한의 정전협정 위반을 공식화한 합참과 유엔사의 입장과 배치된다는 점을 지적하지 않을 수 없다. 합참은 ‘국경선 요새화’ 등 한반도 긴장을 고조시키는 활동의 즉각 중단과 함께 북측의 사과와 책임 있는 조치를 강력히 촉구했다. 만약 이런 요구에 응하지 않으면 향후 군사적 대응에 나설 것이라고 경고했다. 군사 대응을 경고한 것은 북한이 DMZ에 지뢰를 매설한 행위를 불법적인 정전협정 위반 행위이자 도발 행위로 판단하고 있기 때문이다. 그런데 정작 군 통수권자인 이 대통령은 합참의 경고와 맞지 않는 발언을 한 것이다. 이번 사고는 ‘불의의 사고’가 아니라 지뢰 매설이란 도발 행위에 의해 일어난 결과다. 지뢰는 상대방에게 위해를 가하려는 목적으로 매설한다. 북한 관할 구역에 매설했다면 방어용이란 명분이 통하겠지만, 비무장지대에서 그런 일을 한 것은 명백한 도발이다. 왜 도발을 도발이라 규정하지 못하는가. 더구나 한반도의 군사적 긴장을 고조시키는 측은 우리가 아니라 북한이란 점이 이번에 재확인됐다. 군사적 긴장을 낮추는 노력은 북한이 해야 할 일이고, 백번 양보해도 남북이 함께해야 한다. 국경 요새화란 명목으로 군사 긴장을 고조시키는 북한의 도발에 의해 명백한 피해가 발생했고, 앞으로도 일어날 수 있는데도 우리 한쪽만 긴장을 낮추는 조치를 하겠다는 대북 접근법에 공감하는 국민이 얼마나 될지 의문이다. 얼마 전 국회에서 DMZ 지뢰 폭발 당시 아비규환의 현장에서 다친 중사가 부대원들에게 자신보다 더 많이 다친 대대장을 챙기라고 명령한 뒤 사고 현장을 기어서 탈출하는 모습이 담긴 보디캠 영상이 공개됐다. 과연 북한 도발로 부상당한 전우를 지켜본 이들에게 대통령의 발언이 어떻게 들렸을지 생각했으면 한다.
editorial.pullQuote: 이번 사건은 '불의의 사고'가 아니라 지뢰 매설이란 도발 행위에 의해 일어난 결과다.
summary: 이재명 대통령이 DMZ 지뢰 폭발을 '불의의 사고'라 표현해 논란이다.
합참은 북한의 정전협정 위반을 도발로 규정했으나 대통령 발언과 배치된다.
북한 도발로 피해를 입은 장병들을 고려할 때 일방적 긴장 완화는 국민 공감 어렵다.

editorial.titleTr: [Editorial] DMZ Mine Explosion: North Korea's Provocation, Not an Accident
summaryTr: President Lee Jae-myung's characterization of the DMZ landmine explosion as an 'unfortunate accident' has sparked controversy.
The Joint Chiefs of Staff defined North Korea's violation of the armistice agreement as provocation, which contradicts the president's remarks.
Considering the soldiers who suffered damage from North Korean provocation, unilateral tension reduction is difficult to gain public support.
editorial.bodyTr:
President Lee Jae-myung described as an "unexpected accident" yesterday during the Armed Forces Day ceremony an incident in which three South Korean soldiers were seriously wounded ten days earlier by landmines planted by North Korea in the Demilitarized Zone. There was no condemnation of North Korea's violation of the Armistice Agreement, nor any rebuttal to Kim Yo-jong's claim that it was a "false flag operation." Instead, President Lee stated, "The government will consistently pursue substantive measures to lower military tensions between the South and North."

First, it must be pointed out that the President's remarks contradict the positions of the Joint Chiefs of Staff and the United Nations Command, which formalized North Korea's Armistice violation the day before. The Joint Chiefs of Staff strongly urged an immediate halt to activities escalating tensions on the Korean Peninsula, including "border fortification," and demanded an apology and responsible measures from the North. They warned of forthcoming military responses if such demands are not met. The military response warning was issued because the military judged North Korea's landmine placement in the DMZ to be an illegal violation of the Armistice Agreement and a provocation. Yet the President, who commands the military, made remarks inconsistent with the Joint Chiefs' warning. This incident is not an "unexpected accident" but a consequence resulting from the provocative act of landmine placement. Landmines are laid with the intent to cause harm to the other side. If they had been laid in North Korean territory, one could argue they serve a defensive purpose, but doing so in the DMZ is clearly a provocation. Why can the government not call a provocation what it is? Moreover, this incident has reconfirmed that it is North Korea, not South Korea, that is escalating military tensions on the Korean Peninsula. Efforts to reduce military tensions should come from North Korea, and at minimum should be undertaken jointly by both sides. Actual harm has resulted from North Korea's provocations that escalate military tensions under the pretext of border fortification, and further incidents may occur. One wonders how many citizens will be convinced by an approach to the North that seeks to lower tensions on our side alone. Recently, body camera footage from the National Assembly showed a sergeant wounded during the chaotic scene of the DMZ landmine explosion, instructing fellow soldiers to prioritize a more seriously injured battalion commander before crawling away from the scene himself. One hopes the President reflected on how his remarks must have sounded to those who witnessed comrades wounded by North Korean provocation.

leanScore.label: Strongly conservative
leanScore.rationale: 북한의 지뢰 매설을 '불의의 사고'가 아닌 명백한 '도발'로 규정하고, 대북 대화/긴장 완화 정책을 비판하며 군사적 강경 대응과 한미동맹 기반의 안보를 강조하는 보수적 프레임을 일관되게 전개함.

editorial.title: Fact vs. fiction
editorial.body: A controversial film hypothesis raises questions about historical distortion Controversy over “The Assassin(s),” a film about the 1974 shooting death of Yuk Young-soo, wife of then-President Park Chung-hee, has spilled into the political arena. At issue is not artistic license itself, but whether cinematic invention can justify distorting established historical facts. The film depicts the Aug. 15, 1974, shooting and advances a plot hypothesis that people close to Park or the Korean Central Intelligence Agency may have been involved. The filmmakers insist they did not explicitly identify who was behind the assassination. Yet the film invites audiences to entertain the insinuation that Park himself used or was involved in the incident to overcome a political crisis. For his children, the suggestion that their father may have been involved in their mother’s death to preserve his power is an especially grave insult. The historical record does not substantiate the theory. The Special Investigation Headquarters concluded at the time that Moon Se-kwang, acting on orders from North Korea and Jochongnyeon, the pro-Pyongyang federation of Korean residents in Japan, attempted to assassinate Park but missed, with a stray bullet striking and killing the first lady. Questions have been raised over the years, but no evidence has emerged to substantiate the claim that Park orchestrated his wife’s death. Rep. Joo Jin-woo of the opposition People Power Party criticized the film for portraying Park, rather than North Korea, as being behind Yuk’s assassination. He called it a historical distortion, not mere cinematic imagination, and said those involved should be punished. Party leader Jang Dong-hyeok called for a boycott, while Rep. Shin Dong-uk urged that screenings be halted. A former Seoul city council member also filed a criminal complaint against some production staff, accusing them of defaming Park. Yet the ruling Democratic Party of Korea has remained conspicuously silent. Why? Perhaps because the film is doing for the party what it has long done itself: denigrating Park. If a film had used a similarly shocking imagination to disparage former Presidents Kim Dae-jung or Roh Moo-hyun, would the Democratic Party have been so tolerant? It is difficult to imagine it would have been. The party pushed through a law imposing up to five years in prison for spreading false information about the May 18 Democratization Movement, which took place in its traditional stronghold of Jeonnam-Gwangju. Yet when a film raises an unverified theory about Park, the party has nothing to say. The contrast is glaring. It is a double standard. The controversy also recalls the uproar over the Paichai High School baseball team’s “Let’s go to Starbucks” chant during a June 29 game. President Lee Jae Myung lashed out at Starbucks Korea, displaying his remarkable “imagination” by linking its “Tank Day” tumbler promotion for May 18, 2026, with an insult to the May 18 Democratization Movement of 1980. Many saw this as an excessive leap in logic. Nevertheless, some government ministries went so far as to launch a boycott. Chung Yong-jin, chairman of Shinsegae Group, Starbucks Korea’s parent company, apologized publicly, while police conducted a search and seizure at Starbucks Korea. The Seoul-based Paichai team then visited the May 18 National Cemetery in Jeonnam-Gwangju to apologize for its chant. By the same standard, the film’s director, actors and other production staff should at least be prepared to visit Park Chung-hee’s grave, pay their respects and apologize. There is a serious danger when unverified hypotheses become embedded in the public consciousness as hidden truths through the power of a polished commercial film. Cinematic imagination is no substitute for evidence. When fiction is presented as a plausible explanation of established historical facts, especially a national tragedy, criticism of historical distortion is inevitable. Freedom of expression matters. But it is not a license to blur the line between fact and fiction. At the very least, the filmmakers and distributor should apologize to the bereaved family of Park and Yuk and make unmistakably clear to audiences that the film does not depict established historical fact. editorial.bodyTr: 1974년 윤영숙 전 영부인 피격 사망 사건을 다룬 영화 '암살자들'을 둘러싼 논란이 정치권으로 번지고 있다. 문제는 영화적 자유 자체가 아니라, 영화적 허구가 확립된 역사적 사실을 왜곡하는 것을 정당화할 수 있는가 하는 점이다. 이 영화는 1974년 8월 15일의 총격 사건을 묘사하고, 박정희 전 대통령과 가까운 인물들이나 중앙정보부가 관여했을 가능성을 제시하는 음모론을 제기한다. 영화제작진은 암살의 배후를 명시적으로 밝히지 않았다고 주장하지만, 영화는 박 전 대통령이 정치 위기를 극복하기 위해 이 사건을 이용했거나 관여했을 가능성을 관객들에게 암시한다. 그의 자녀들에게 아버지가 권력 유지를 위해 어머니의 죽음에 연루되었을 가능성이라는 주장은 특히 심각한 모욕이다. 역사적 기록은 이 이론을 뒷받침하지 않는다. 당시 특별수사본부는 문세광이 북한과 재일본조선인총연합회의 지령을 받아 박 전 대통령을 암살하려다 실패했으며, 유탄이 영부인을 맞았다고 결론지었다. 수십 년에 걸쳐 의문이 제기되어 왔지만, 박 전 대통령이 아내의 죽음을 조작했다는 주장을 뒷받침할 증거는 나타나지 않았다. 야당 국민의힘 주진우 의원은 영화가 북한이 아닌 박 전 대통령을 윤영숙 암살의 배후로 묘사한다며 이를 영화적 상상이 아닌 역사 왜곡이라고 비판했고, 관련자들의 처벌을 촉구했다. 장동혁 당대표는 불매운동을 촉구했고, 신동욱 의원은 상영 중단을 촉구했다. 서울의 한 전직 시의원도 제작진 일부를 상대로 박 전 대통령을 모욕했다는 혐의로 고소했다. 그러나 여당인 민주당은 눈에 띄게 침묵하고 있다. 왜일까? 아마도 이 영화가 민주당이 오랫동안 해온 일, 즉 박정희를 폄하하는 것을 대신해주기 때문일 수 있다. 만약 어떤 영화가 비슷한 충격적인 상상력으로 김대중이나 노무현 전 대통령을 훼손했다면, 민주당이 그렇게 관대했을까? 그럴 가능성은 거의 없어 보인다. 민주당은 전통적 기반인 호남의 5·18민주화운동에 대해 거짓정보를 유포한 자에게 최대 5년의 징역을 부과하는 법안을 통과시켰다. 그런데 박 전 대통령에 관해 검증되지 않은 이론을 제기하는 영화에 대해서는 아무말도 하지 않는다. 그 대조는 너무나 뚜렷하다. 이것은 이중 기준이다. 이 논란은 또한 6월 29일 경기의 배재고 야구팀의 "스타벅스 가자" 응원가 소동을 떠올리게 한다. 이준석 대표는 스타벅스 코리아를 맹비난하며, 2026년 5월 18일 "탱크데이" 텀블러 프로모션을 1980년 5·18민주화운동에 대한 모욕으로 연결지으려는 놀라운 "상상력"을 발휘했다. 많은 사람들이 이를 과도한 논리의 비약으로 봤다. 그럼에도 불구하고 일부 정부 부처는 불매운동까지 벌였다. 스타벅스 코리아의 모회사인 신세계그룹 정용진 회장은 공개 사과했고, 경찰은 스타벅스 코리아에 대해 수색·압수를 실시했다. 배재고 야구팀은 이후 응원가에 대해 사과하기 위해 전남 광주의 5·18국립묘지를 방문했다. 같은 기준으로 따지면, 영화 감독과 배우, 제작진 등은 최소한 박정희 전 대통령의 묘소를 찾아 참배하고 사과할 준비를 해야 한다. 검증되지 않은 가설이 정교하게 만들어진 상업 영화의 힘을 통해 대중의 의식 속에 숨겨진 진실로 자리 잡을 때 심각한 위험이 생긴다. 영화적 상상력은 증거를 대체할 수 없다. 픽션이 확립된 역사적 사실, 특히 국가적 비극의 그럴듯한 설명으로 제시될 때, 역사 왜곡에 대한 비판은 불가피하다. 표현의 자유는 중요하다. 하지만 그것이 사실과 허구의 경계를 흐릿하게 만드는 면허증은 아니다. 최소한 영화 제작진과 배급사는 박정희 전 대통령과 윤영숙 여사의 유족에게 사과하고, 이 영화가 확립된 역사적 사실을 묘사하지 않는다는 점을 관객들에게 명확히 해야 한다.

editorials.title: Fact vs. fiction
editorials.body: A controversial film hypothesis raises questions about historical distortion Controversy over “The Assassin(s),” a film about the 1974 shooting death of Yuk Young-soo, wife of then-President Park Chung-hee, has spilled into the political arena. At issue is not artistic license itself, but whether cinematic invention can justify distorting established historical facts. The film depicts the Aug. 15, 1974, shooting and advances a plot hypothesis that people close to Park or the Korean Central Intelligence Agency may have been involved. The filmmakers insist they did not explicitly identify who was behind the assassination. Yet the film invites audiences to entertain the insinuation that Park himself used or was involved in the incident to overcome a political crisis. For his children, the suggestion that their father may have been involved in their mother’s death to preserve his power is an especially grave insult. The historical record does not substantiate the theory. The Special Investigation Headquarters concluded at the time that Moon Se-kwang, acting on orders from North Korea and Jochongnyeon, the pro-Pyongyang federation of Korean residents in Japan, attempted to assassinate Park but missed, with a stray bullet striking and killing the first lady. Questions have been raised over the years, but no evidence has emerged to substantiate the claim that Park orchestrated his wife’s death. Rep. Joo Jin-woo of the opposition People Power Party criticized the film for portraying Park, rather than North Korea, as being behind Yuk’s assassination. He called it a historical distortion, not mere cinematic imagination, and said those involved should be punished. Party leader Jang Dong-hyeok called for a boycott, while Rep. Shin Dong-uk urged that screenings be halted. A former Seoul city council member also filed a criminal complaint against some production staff, accusing them of defaming Park. Yet the ruling Democratic Party of Korea has remained conspicuously silent. Why? Perhaps because the film is doing for the party what it has long done itself: denigrating Park. If a film had used a similarly shocking imagination to disparage former Presidents Kim Dae-jung or Roh Moo-hyun, would the Democratic Party have been so tolerant? It is difficult to imagine it would have been. The party pushed through a law imposing up to five years in prison for spreading false information about the May 18 Democratization Movement, which took place in its traditional stronghold of Jeonnam-Gwangju. Yet when a film raises an unverified theory about Park, the party has nothing to say. The contrast is glaring. It is a double standard. The controversy also recalls the uproar over the Paichai High School baseball team’s “Let’s go to Starbucks” chant during a June 29 game. President Lee Jae Myung lashed out at Starbucks Korea, displaying his remarkable “imagination” by linking its “Tank Day” tumbler promotion for May 18, 2026, with an insult to the May 18 Democratization Movement of 1980. Many saw this as an excessive leap in logic. Nevertheless, some government ministries went so far as to launch a boycott. Chung Yong-jin, chairman of Shinsegae Group, Starbucks Korea’s parent company, apologized publicly, while police conducted a search and seizure at Starbucks Korea. The Seoul-based Paichai team then visited the May 18 National Cemetery in Jeonnam-Gwangju to apologize for its chant. By the same standard, the film’s director, actors and other production staff should at least be prepared to visit Park Chung-hee’s grave, pay their respects and apologize. There is a serious danger when unverified hypotheses become embedded in the public consciousness as hidden truths through the power of a polished commercial film. Cinematic imagination is no substitute for evidence. When fiction is presented as a plausible explanation of established historical facts, especially a national tragedy, criticism of historical distortion is inevitable. Freedom of expression matters. But it is not a license to blur the line between fact and fiction. At the very least, the filmmakers and distributor should apologize to the bereaved family of Park and Yuk and make unmistakably clear to audiences that the film does not depict established historical fact. editorial.bodyTr: President Donald Trump announced on the 1st that he would proceed with South Korea's investment in Alaska liquefied natural gas projects as if it were a done deal. However, the fact sheets released by our government and the U.S. Commerce Department do not specify the investment amount or whether the investment has been confirmed.
